1	# Entire for Orca: plan
2	
3	Bring Entire (trails, findings, approvals, checkpoints) into Orca's UI as an Orca plugin, the way
4	Orca already surfaces GitHub pull requests and checks.
5	
6	Status: phases 0 and 0.5 done, and a stopgap Entire panel works from a development folder. Next:
7	phase 1 spikes.
8	
9	## Environment
10	
11	- Orca desktop runs on Windows (1.4.245). Plugins are in alpha: manifest format 2, host API 1.0.
12	- Most Orca and Entire projects live in WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`). Orca also has an SSH host.
13	- Entire CLI `0.12.3-nightly` on both sides: WSL (keyring login) and Windows in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
14	  (Credential Manager login).
15	- This repo: `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, origin
16	  `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/et/entire-repos/orca-entire-extension`, Entire enabled.
17	
18	## What Orca's plugin API allows today (1.4.245)
19	
20	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
21	
22	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
23	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
24	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
25	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
26	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
27	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
28	  `settings.*` (worker only).
29	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
30	- The command palette ignores a command's return value. The Run button in Settings → Plugins shows its
31	  first 200 characters in a toast. Worker stdout and stderr go to the plugin's Logs (last 200 lines).
32	- Panels are sealed: Orca injects CSP `connect-src 'none'` (scripts and styles inline only, images
33	  as data URLs), blocks links and `window.open`, and gives a panel no channel to its own worker. A
34	  panel can call only `workspace.readContext` and `notifications.show`, and loads one HTML file.
35	- Stopgap: Orca rereads a development folder's panel file whenever the folder changes and remounts
36	  the panel when the HTML differs. Writing a file there neither restarts the worker nor asks for
37	  approval again (only shortcuts and VM recipes tie approval to file bytes). So the worker writes its
38	  data into the panel file. Installed copies are hash-checked and refused once a byte changes, so
39	  this works only from a development folder.
40	- Stopgap for the panel's ↻: a panel's only mutation is `notifications.show`, which Orca records in
41	  `plugins-data\audit.log` as `titleChars=<n>`. The button shows a notification with a title length
42	  no worker notice uses, and a running worker watches the log. Orca's 5-minute idle timer resets on
43	  the worker's own host calls, so once started the worker calls `readContext` every 5 seconds and
44	  stays up with Orca. A keyboard shortcut is no way out: in
45	  a development folder, keybindings tie approval to every file, so each panel write would need a new
46	  review.
47	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
48	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
49	- The installed build has no `orca plugin ...` CLI (it is on Orca's `main`). Load the plugin through
50	  Settings → Plugins → Development folders.
51	- On 1.4.245 the manifest must keep `publisher` (leaving it out needs `>=1.4.246`). When distributing,
52	  it must equal the GitHub owner of the repository Orca installs from. Ids may not start with `orca-`.
53	
54	## Spike results (2026-10-30)
55	
56	Run from Windows Node with the worker's env allowlist:
57	
58	- `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire trail list ... --json` works with the WSL
59	  login, in 0.6–0.8 s per call.
60	- Orca's CLI (`resources\bin\orca.exe` beside the app) works once APPDATA is derived from USERPROFILE.
61	  `worktree list` takes about 2.1 s.
62	- `readContext` terminal ids are Orca CLI terminal handles. `orca terminal show --terminal <id> --json`
63	  returns the workspace's `worktreePath` (e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\peterc\ccw`), which gives the
64	  distro and Linux path.
65	- Entire has `--json` on `status`, `trail list/show/approvals/finding`, and `trail watch --json`
66	  (the trail's SSE stream as JSON lines). `trail show` exits 1 when the branch has no trail.
67	
68	## Architecture
69	
70	- One `trusted-worker` plugin. The worker is the only part that talks to Entire.
71	- Find the focused workspace's path: first terminal handle from `readContext` → `orca terminal show`.
72	  Fallback: match branch and name against `orca worktree list`. This is a stopgap until `readContext`
73	  carries a path (see the asks below).
74	- Run Entire where the repo and its login live. For a WSL path, use
75	  `wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <path> -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire ...`. For a local path, run
76	  `entire` directly. SSH workspaces come later.
77	- Shell out to the Entire CLI rather than calling its REST API. The CLI owns login, contexts and cell
78	  routing, so the plugin never holds a token. `entire api` covers gaps.
79	- Refresh the focused workspace on `agent.status.changed`, when focus moves to it (no event says so:
80	  the worker polls `readContext` every 5 seconds) and every 5 minutes. The 5-minute and agent
81	  refreshes write the panel only when Entire's data changed, since each write remounts it; after a
82	  switch the panel shows "Checking…" until the worker rewrites it. Later, tail
83	  `trail watch --json` while the worker is alive.
84	- Panels only render what the worker hands them. Today that is the panel file the worker writes
85	  (`panel/entire.html`, up to 10 workspaces, matched to the focused one by terminal id, then name
86	  and branch). Swap to the panel → worker channel when Orca ships it. Feature-detect with
87	  `orca.host.has(...)` so one build runs on shipped and newer Orca.
88	- Entire text (intent, findings, comments) is untrusted: render it as text and never execute it.
89	
90	## GitHub feature → Entire equivalent
91	
92	| Orca + GitHub today             | Entire equivalent                                  | Unblocked by                     |
93	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
94	| PR and CI notifications         | trail events → notifications                       | shipped API                      |
95	| Create, approve, merge a PR     | `trail create`, `approve`, `merge` as commands     | shipped API                      |
96	| Checks sidebar, review comments | trail panel: gates, CI runs, findings, approvals   | Orca #25256                      |
97	| Issues on Tasks → new workspace | trails tab → start a workspace on the change       | Orca #26282                      |
98	| PR badge on the workspace card  | trail badge on the card                            | #26282, then a forge provider    |
99	
100	For `et/` repos (`entire://` remotes, like this one) Orca has no forge integration at all, so this
101	plugin is the only one. For GitHub repos it sits beside Orca's GitHub support.
102	
103	## Phases
104	
105	- [x] 0. Repo on Windows, Entire enabled in WSL and on Windows, project added to Orca.
106	- [x] 0.5 Smoke test: load the dev plugin and run **Entire: Check connection** in a WSL workspace and in
107	      this one. Both reported connected in a Windows notification.
108	- [ ] 1. Spikes: real trail JSON fixtures (create a test trail), `trail watch` through `wsl.exe` versus
109	      the 5-minute reaper, the plugin consent flow, latency budget.
110	- [ ] 2. v0.1 on shipped Orca: commands (show trail, findings, approve, merge, create, refresh) and
111	      notifications when an agent finishes and on trail events.
112	- [ ] 3. Trail panel. A stopgap panel (repo status, the trail and its merge gates, recent
113	      checkpoints, connection check, a ↻ that works while the worker runs) works from a development
114	      folder. Trail #1 links `plugin-scaffold`; its JSON is `test/fixtures/trail-show.json`, and a
115	      reviewed, merged change is `test/fixtures/trail-367-*.json`. The Trail section follows Entire's
116	      web view (change, code review, merge gates, findings) from `trail show` and `trail finding list`,
117	      plus `git diff --shortstat` for the line counts. Not shown: the web view's Confidence, Risk,
118	      Drift and Security scores, which no CLI command or API type exposes. A live, installable panel
119	      needs a panel → worker channel (Orca #25256).
120	- [ ] 4. Trails tab on the Tasks page and a settings form (Orca #26282).
121	- [ ] 5. Deeper: status bar item, forge provider for `entire://` remotes, Entire agent hooks and skills,
122	      checkpoints, `entire why`, `entire review`.
123	- [ ] 6. Distribution: a GitHub mirror (Orca installs over https Git and derives the publisher from the
124	      owner), then a catalog listing.
125	
126	## Asks for the Orca team
127	
128	1. A channel from a panel to its own worker (#25256, or a push channel). It blocks any live panel.
129	2. `workspace.readContext`: add the worktree id, path and host (local, WSL, SSH).
130	3. Task sources and plugin settings (#26282), with a start recipe that can check out an existing branch.
131	4. Status bar items and sidebar cards (#23143, #26951).
132	5. Opening external URLs from panels and workers (#27568).
133	6. Long-lived worker subscriptions: the 5-minute idle reaper stops `trail watch`.
134	7. A way to run a command on the workspace's host (WSL, SSH) from a worker.
135	
136	## Risks and open questions
137	
138	- Phases 3–5 depend on unmerged Orca PRs: #25256 quiet since Oct 7, #26282 active, #15315 (forge
139	  providers) stale since August.
140	- The WSL bridge does not cover SSH workspaces.
141	- Both sides run Entire 0.12.3-nightly. On Windows, `entire status` reports this repo's 7 Codex hooks
142	  as needing trust approval in Codex (`/hooks`); that only matters when using Codex here.
143	  `entire agent add codex` and `entire doctor` rewrite committed hook files, so run them on a branch.
144	- A worker's PATH comes from Orca's environment at launch. Restart Orca after installing Entire on
145	  Windows.
146	- Can #26282's start recipe check out an existing branch, or only branch off a base?
147

# agent-desktop

agent-desktop is a CLI that lets an AI agent observe and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. It is a tool, not an agent. Every command prints one JSON envelope (`ok`, `data` or `error`). The observe, act and verify loop runs in you.

## Shell syntax

Examples use a POSIX shell. In PowerShell, quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e1'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. Use `$env:NAME = 'value'` instead of `export`, and `| ConvertFrom-Json` instead of `$(...)` and `jq`. The Windows skill has the PowerShell forms.

## First run

1. Run `agent-desktop status`. It reports the platform, permissions and `supported_surfaces`.
2. Run `agent-desktop skills get platform`. It loads the skill for the OS the binary runs on (macOS, Windows or Linux).
3. For flags and syntax, run `agent-desktop <command> --help`. This skill does not repeat flag lists.

## The loop

Use `find` when you know the role or exact name. Otherwise map the app first and drill into one region.

```
agent-desktop snapshot --skeleton --app "Notes" -i --compact   # shallow map, children_count on cut branches
agent-desktop snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact        # drill into one region
agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e12                              # act on a qualified ref
agent-desktop snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact        # verify: re-read the same region
```

- A small app needs no skeleton. Take a full `snapshot -i`.
- Never skeleton a surface (`--surface menu`, `sheet`, `alert`). A surface is already focused.
- An action that opens a menu, sheet or alert lists it in `data.surfaces`. Target that overlay next.
- After an async step, use `wait` (see `commands-system.md`). A fixed sleep is a race.

## Refs

- Output refs are qualified: `@<snapshot_id>:e<N>`, for example `@s8f3k2p9:e1`. Pass them to later commands as they are.
- Refs are valid for one snapshot. After any UI change, re-drill the affected region or take a new snapshot.
- Only addressable elements get refs. Static text and inert containers do not.
- `STALE_REF`: the ref no longer matches the live UI. Take a fresh snapshot and use the new ref.
- `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: more than one live element matches. Narrow the target with `find --role --name --exact` or `--root`, then use the new ref.
- `SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND`: the snapshot id expired. Snapshot again.

## Delivery and retry

Action results carry `data.disposition` and errors carry `error.disposition`, each with `delivery` and `retry`. Observation commands such as `snapshot` have none on success; their errors, and every `INVALID_ARGS` refusal, carry `not_delivered` and `retry: safe`.

- Retry or substitute an action only when `disposition.retry` is `safe`. Only `not_delivered` is safe.
- Any other delivery value means the action may have landed. A repeat can click, type or submit twice, and `toggle` can undo itself.
- On a result that is not safe, read the live state (`get`, `is`, or a fresh snapshot) and decide from that. `details.post_state` helps when present.
- Branch on `error.code` and `error.disposition`. Message and suggestion text can change.
- `details.retryable: false` means waiting cannot change the outcome. Try a different approach.

## Headless and headed

Ref actions are headless by default. They use semantic accessibility calls and do not take focus, move the cursor, synthesize keys or use the clipboard. If no semantic path exists, the action fails closed. Use the global `--headed` flag only when the user explicitly permits physical input, such as double-click, hover, drag, or focus. Never switch to headed mode to recover from a headless failure. Raw coordinates (`--xy`) never imply focus. Which actions need `--headed` differs by OS: read the platform skill.

## References

Load one only when you need it: `agent-desktop skills get desktop <reference>`.

| Reference | Open it when |
|-----------|--------------|
| `commands-observation` | You need `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` semantics, partial trees, or the `--root` rules |
| `commands-interaction` | You choose between click, type, set-value, select, toggle, scroll, press and mouse commands, or you debug an action error |
| `commands-system` | You launch or close apps, manage windows, use the clipboard, `wait`, `batch`, sessions, multi-agent cursors, tracing, or load skills |
| `workflows` | You want worked patterns (forms, menus, dialogs, waiting for a new window, scroll-find, drag) and the anti-patterns list |

The panel now loads for your VPS workspaces. I ran the new code inside `Orca.exe` with the harness, and all 54 tests pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**Why it didn't load:** VPS workspaces live on the paired "Endo VPS Server" Orca runtime, not on your desktop's. When you clicked them, Orca told the plugin only the repo's name, with no branch, terminals or path. The worker searched only local workspaces, so it found nothing.

**What the worker does now:**
- **Finding the workspace:** if nothing local matches, it asks each paired server for its repos and worktrees and matches the repo name (`src/worker/workspace.mjs`).
- **Reading Entire:** it can't run anything on the VPS. Orca's SSH key needs a passphrase, no ssh-agent holds it, and Orca's CLI can only run commands there by opening terminal tabs. Instead, the Windows `entire` reads trails and findings from Entire's server using the repo's origin URL and branch (`src/worker/snapshot.mjs`, `src/worker/hosts.mjs`).
- **Panel:** it shows the real branch and "Endo VPS Server /home/…". Repo status, checkpoints and the diff need the checkout on the VPS, so those sections say "Only readable on Endo VPS Server" instead of showing an error.

**Harness results:**
- **endo.chat_backend** (`fix/issue-620-root-token-followups`) found trail #376 in about 3.5 s.
- **leadgen** shows "repository not on Entire for this computer's login". It really isn't on Entire: the server answers 404.

**To try it in Orca:** the running worker still has the old code. Turn the plugin off and on in Settings → Plugins, then switch to a VPS workspace.

**Limits:**
- If one repo on the VPS has two or more worktrees, the plugin can't tell which one is focused, and the panel says so. Fixing that needs Orca's `readContext` to include the workspace path, which is already on our list of asks for the Orca team.
- Repo status and checkpoints for the VPS would need a way to run commands there. One option is to start the Windows ssh-agent and add your passphrase-protected `id_vps` key. I haven't done that because it's a system change for you to decide on; say if you want it.

I also updated `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/PLAN.md`, and added a `repo <name>` harness scenario, e.g. `node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs repo leadgen`. I left a read-only sparse clone of Orca's source in `%TEMP%\orca-src` for reference.
